diagnosedFailures.observed: Build an 8-lesson Spanish for Healthcare Professionals course was previewed as Spanish.
diagnosedFailures.rootCause: The prompt-title parser treated every for/with phrase as a generic brief qualifier even when it belonged to the course name.
diagnosedFailures.repair: Only syntactically explicit brief boundaries are trimmed; meaningful for/with title phrases remain intact.

diagnosedFailures.observed: Valid exported lesson plans showed their timing rows but the quality grader reported 0 minutes and blocked ZIP export.
diagnosedFailures.rootCause: The deep grader counted only lines ending in minutes while the exporter preserved ordinary min/mins abbreviations.
diagnosedFailures.repair: Grader 1.10.20 accepts min, mins, minute, and minutes without weakening the exact requested-session-clock check.
regressions: 10 min + 15 mins + 25 minutes is accepted for a requested 50-minute lesson
A genuinely mismatched 110-minute outline remains a P0
Representative four-material ZIP and selected-two-material ZIP both download and pass content audit

diagnosedFailures.observed: Four export tests declared 75-minute lessons while their fixture outlines supplied only 20 to 60 minutes.
diagnosedFailures.rootCause: The stronger timing gate made old synthetic workspaces honestly unready.
diagnosedFailures.repair: Fixtures now contain complete 75-minute instructional outlines instead of bypassing the readiness contract.

diagnosedFailures.observed: The control was visible with the precise accessible name Open Course Map full-screen preview while the test still searched for the obsolete generic name Full screen.
diagnosedFailures.rootCause: The accessibility label improved but the interaction test retained the older title-based selector.
diagnosedFailures.repair: The test now uses the visible control's precise accessible name and verifies the 390 by 844 dialog owns the viewport.

claimBoundary: This is deterministic and fixture-backed Chromium interaction evidence for the V0.16.60 release candidate. It verifies rendered states, responsive behavior, accessibility selectors, readiness gates, exporter completion, ZIP contents, and failure recovery. It is not a fresh live Gemma browser generation, human usability study, accessibility conformance audit, classroom validation, universal device-performance result, adapter win, or paid-reference parity claim.
